item.title: Grokking Algorithms
item.description: In Aditya Y. Bhargava’s diagrams, you can watch binary search discard half the possibilities at each step. That gives big-O notation a concrete example before you reach the code.

item.title: Obsidian
item.description: A folder of Markdown files, a short list of starting points and links between notes.

item.title: Three pieces for an Obsidian outline
item.description: Two plugins and a CSS snippet for moving through a note one branch at a time.

item.title: What I watch after a deploy
item.description: A small Datadog query, a personal alert and a link back to the exact window can answer a question raised by a change.

item.title: When a failed scan looks like a closed job
item.description: A missing vacancy can mean the employer closed it or the scanner stopped early. TechJobsNL needs enough evidence to tell the difference.

item.title: Why a folded bullet lost its place in Obsidian
item.description: Roamer drew an outline guide in the right place until someone folded the item. The fix came from measuring the second render.

item.title: Grokking Algorithms
item.description: Reading notes on the illustrated explanations of algorithms in Aditya Y. Bhargava’s second edition.

item.title: Fixing Automatic Rotation on a Lenovo Yoga 7 2-in-1 with Fedora
item.description: Fedora could not see the Yoga 7 14ILL10 accelerometer. Installing Lenovo's model-specific ISH firmware brought it back.

item.title: herdr
item.description: Using herdr with Ghostty on Mac and Windows Terminal on Windows.

item.title: How to Get Roam-Style Bullet Navigation in Obsidian
item.description: How to replicate the click-to-zoom outliner interaction from Roam, RemNote, and Logseq in Obsidian, with two plugins and a CSS snippet for styled bullets.

item.title: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP): Narrow the Contract
item.description: A shared contract that grows to serve everyone ends up serving no one well. Learn how ISP keeps each interface honest about what its client actually needs.

item.title: How I Use Obsidian as a Thinking Studio
item.description: How I configured Obsidian as a developer's personal thinking studio — vault structure, web clipper, key plugins, and the PKM ideas behind each decision.

item.title: Hot Path: How to Identify and Optimize It in .NET
item.description: A hot path is code that runs on every request — small inefficiencies there compound into P99 spikes users actually feel. How to find hot paths with profilers and fix them in .NET.

item.title: P50, P95, P99, and the Average: What Latency Numbers Actually Tell You
item.description: Average response time hides the worst user experiences. P99 can run 100× slower than P50 on the same dataset. What P50, P95, and P99 mean, why they matter, and how to read them together.

item.title: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP): Depend on Abstractions
item.description: When business logic knows which database it's talking to, the database owns the business logic. Learn how DIP breaks that grip by making policy depend on what it needs, not on how it's delivered.

item.title: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP): Keep the Promise
item.description: A subtype that can't fully honor its parent's contract doesn't announce itself — it waits. Learn how LSP ensures the contract you depend on is the contract you actually get.

item.title: Open Closed Principle (OCP): Extend Without Breaking
item.description: Code that has to be opened every time requirements change is code you will eventually break. Learn how OCP lets new behavior arrive as new files, not as edits to existing ones.
